case_name: Fagu Manjhi and Others v State of Bihar and Another
respondent:
State of Bihar and Another
Supreme Court of India

14 November 2000
Cr.A. No. 411 of 2000
The Order of the Court was as follows:
1.  Ten persons were convicted for murdering one Begru Manjhi under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code and all were sentenced to imprisonment for life. All of them filed an appeal before the High Court and while the appeal was pending Jailal Manjhi died.
2. So, the appeal was heard in respect of the remaining nine convicted persons. A Division Bench of the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence of all those nine persons. Some days after the High Court's judgment was pronounced, one more convicted person died and his name is Ruplal Manjhi. Out of the remaining 8 persons, three did not file any appeal along with the present appellants. Those three are A-2 Santu Manjhi, A-3 Gaya Manjhi and A-4 Sukdeo Manjhi. Later when Santu Manjhi, A-2 came to know of the filing of the present appeal, he sent a petition

statutes.act: Read With Section 149 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: Ten persons were convicted for murdering one Begru Manjhi under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code and all were sentenced to imprisonment for life.
All of them filed an appeal before the High Court and while the appeal was pending Jailal Manjhi died.
A Division Bench of the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence of all those nine persons.
Some days after the High Court's judgment was pronounced, one more convicted person died and his name is Ruplal Manjhi.
Out of the remaining 8 persons, three did not file any appeal along with the present appellants.
issues: Whether the five appellants shared the common object of murdering Begru Manjhi
petitioner_arguments: The degree of involvement of the present appellants is uncertain and they should be given the benefit of doubt
court_reasoning: Even if some other persons also ran behind those three assailants, it is a very difficult exercise for the Court to conclude that those other persons who ran behind the three assailants shared the common object of murdering the deceased.
The medical evidence in this case shows that all the injuries sustained by the deceased could be attributed to the actions alleged against the aforesaid three persons.
holding: We allow the appeal filed by these five appellants and set aside the conviction and sentence passed on them.
We direct them to be released from jail forthwith unless they are required in any other case.
